name: Tolerance for Semantic Ambiguity
description: Assesses the text's willingness to leave concepts open-ended, paradoxical, or unresolved.
mechanism: Human thought naturally tolerates, and often thrives on, unresolved paradoxes, lingering questions, and intentional semantic ambiguity (e.g., 'Perhaps the answer is unknowable; we just have to live with the contradiction'). AI models, particularly those optimized for instruction-following, are architecturally hostile to ambiguity. Their primary objective function is to collapse probability distributions into singular, defined, 'helpful' answers. They compulsively attempt to resolve or neatly categorize paradoxical concepts. This tool measures the presence and duration of unresolved abstract tensions within the text. If every introduced conflict is immediately met with a neat, triangulated resolution ('However, by balancing X and Y...'), the text is flagged for algorithmic intolerance to ambiguity.
parameters:
Analysis: Semantic Conflict & Resolution Mapping
Metric: Unresolved Tension vs. Immediate Categorization Ratio
Output: 0-100 Algorithmically Forced Resolution Score
accuracy: High — 80-85% when targeted strictly at literary, philosophical, or deep-form essay content.
source: Pragmatic linguistics and LLM alignment behavior research.
useCase: Piercing through AI attempts to write philosophy, creative fiction, or deeply personal reflections that require nuance and unresolved human tension.
strengths:
• Strikes at the core difference between human existential thought and machine optimization logic.
• Highly effective at detecting AI 'thought leadership' articles that try to sound profound but ultimately revert to safe corporate bullet points.
• Resists prompt engineering; telling an AI to 'be ambiguous' usually results in forced, mathematically dense confusion rather than natural lingering paradox.
limitations:
• Prone to false positives on technical manuals, math proofs, or legal texts where absolute clarity and resolution are mandatory.
• Requires massive semantic processing overhead to map conceptual tension across long paragraphs.
• Ineffective on brief, transactional text fragments.

references.title: Jawahar, G. et al. (2020). Automatic Detection of Machine Generated Text: A Critical Survey. COLING.
